description: VTU CSE Practical & Enterprise Case Studies Database

case_studies.subject: BCS403
entities: EMPLOYEE (Ssn, Fname, Lname, Bdate, Address, Sex, Salary, Super_ssn, Dno)
DEPARTMENT (Dnumber, Dname, Mgr_ssn, Mgr_start_date)
PROJECT (Pnumber, Pname, Plocation, Dnum)
DEPENDENT (Essn, Dependent_name, Sex, Bdate, Relationship)
relationships: WORKS_FOR (EMPLOYEE N : 1 DEPARTMENT)
MANAGES (EMPLOYEE 1 : 1 DEPARTMENT)
CONTROLS (DEPARTMENT 1 : N PROJECT)
WORKS_ON (EMPLOYEE M : N PROJECT with attribute Hours)
DEPENDENTS_OF (EMPLOYEE 1 : N DEPENDENT identifying relationship)
case_studies.inputs: Company organization chart, department budget codes, project schedules
case_studies.outputs: Conceptual ER Diagram and Normalized 3NF/BCNF Relational Tables
case_studies.constraints: Every department must have exactly one manager; an employee works for exactly one department
case_studies.source: Elmasri Navathe DBMS Chapter 3 / VTU BCS403 Module 1 Question Bank

case_studies.subject: BCS403
case_studies.scenario: Hospital Patient Care and Ward Management System
entities: PATIENT (Patient_id, Name, DOB, Contact, Blood_group, Emergency_contact)
DOCTOR (Doctor_id, Name, Specialization, License_number, Department_id)
WARD (Ward_number, Ward_type, Total_beds, Available_beds)
APPOINTMENT (Appt_id, Patient_id, Doctor_id, Appt_date, Diagnosis)
relationships: TREATS (DOCTOR 1 : N PATIENT)
ASSIGNED_TO (PATIENT N : 1 WARD with Bed_number, Admission_date)
SCHEDULES (PATIENT 1 : N APPOINTMENT with DOCTOR)
case_studies.inputs: Patient medical history records, doctor shift schedules, ward occupancy registers
case_studies.outputs: Normalized 3NF Healthcare Database Schema and Integrity Constraints
case_studies.constraints: A patient cannot be admitted to multiple beds simultaneously; doctor specialization must match appointment department
case_studies.source: Silberschatz Database System Concepts Chapter 2 / BCS403 Case Studies

case_studies.subject: BCS403
case_studies.scenario: Banking Enterprise Distributed Transaction & ACID Compliance
entities: ACCOUNT (Acc_number, Cust_id, Acc_type, Balance, Branch_code)
CUSTOMER (Cust_id, Name, Phone, Aadhaar, Pan_number)
TRANSACTION (Txn_id, Source_acc, Dest_acc, Amount, Timestamp, Txn_type, Status)
relationships: OWNS (CUSTOMER 1 : N ACCOUNT)
PERFORMS (ACCOUNT 1 : N TRANSACTION)
case_studies.inputs: Concurrent fund transfer requests: Txn 1 transfers Rs 5000 from A to B; Txn 2 reads balance of B
case_studies.outputs: Strict Two-Phase Locking (Strict 2PL) schedule preventing dirty reads and lost updates with WAL logging
case_studies.constraints: Balance >= Minimum_balance (Rs 1000); total money invariant conserved across accounts
case_studies.source: Elmasri Navathe DBMS Chapter 21 / VTU BCS403 Module 4 Notes

case_studies.subject: BCS303
case_studies.scenario: Banker's Algorithm Deadlock Avoidance in Multiprogramming OS
entities: Processes P0 through P4
Resource types A (10 instances), B (5 instances), C (7 instances)
relationships: Allocation Matrix: current resources held by processes
Max Matrix: maximum future claims
Need Matrix: Need[i,j] = Max[i,j] - Allocation[i,j]
case_studies.inputs: Available vector = [3, 3, 2], Allocation and Max matrices for 5 processes
case_studies.outputs: Safe sequence <P1, P3, P4, P0, P2> guaranteeing absence of deadlock
case_studies.constraints: Work vector >= Need[i] before allocating resources to Pi
case_studies.source: Silberschatz OS Concepts Chapter 8 / BCS303 Module 3

case_studies.subject: BCS303
case_studies.scenario: Demand Paging and Page Replacement Under High Memory Pressure
entities: Physical Memory Frames: Frame 0 through Frame 3 (4 frames total)
Process Virtual Page Reference String: 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3, 0, 3, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 7, 0, 1
relationships: Page Table: Maps Virtual Page Number (VPN) to Physical Frame Number (PFN) with Valid/Invalid bit
Page Fault Handler: Traps to OS kernel on Invalid bit access, swaps page in from swap partition
case_studies.inputs: Reference string with 20 memory accesses, compare FIFO vs LRU vs Optimal replacement policies
case_studies.outputs: Page fault counts: Optimal = 9 faults, LRU = 12 faults, FIFO = 15 faults (Demonstrates Belady's Anomaly risk)
case_studies.constraints: Thrashing condition occurs if sum of working sets exceeds available physical frames
case_studies.source: Silberschatz OS Concepts Chapter 10 / BCS303 Module 4

case_studies.subject: BCS502
case_studies.scenario: Campus Network OSPF Link-State Routing Deployment
entities: Core Layer 3 Switches (Backbone Area 0)
Distribution Routers (Engineering Area 1, Admin Area 2, Hostel Area 3)
relationships: Link-State Advertisements (LSA) flooded within non-backbone areas
Area Border Routers (ABR) summarize routes into Backbone Area 0
case_studies.outputs: Converged Shortest Path First (SPF) routing table with zero routing loops and fast sub-second failover
case_studies.constraints: All non-backbone areas must physically or virtually connect to Area 0
case_studies.source: Forouzan Data Communications Chapter 20 / BCS502 Module 3

case_studies.subject: BCS502
case_studies.scenario: TCP Congestion Control Dynamics in High-Bandwidth Latency-Sensitive WAN
entities: Sender TCP Stack (Congestion Window cwnd, Slow Start Threshold ssthresh)
Receiver TCP Stack (Advertised Receive Window rwnd)
Intermediate Bottleneck Router (Buffer capacity 64 packets)
relationships: Slow Start Phase: cwnd doubles every RTT (exponential growth)
Congestion Avoidance Phase: cwnd increases by 1 MSS every RTT (additive increase)
Fast Retransmit & Fast Recovery (TCP Reno): On 3 duplicate ACKs, ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd = ssthresh + 3
case_studies.inputs: Transmission of 100MB file over 1 Gbps link with 50ms RTT and 0.1% packet loss
case_studies.outputs: Throughput analysis comparing TCP Tahoe (resets cwnd to 1 on packet loss) vs TCP Reno (Fast Recovery)
case_studies.constraints: Effective window = min(cwnd, rwnd) prevents receiver buffer overflow
case_studies.source: Kurose & Ross Computer Networking Chapter 3 / BCS502 M4

case_studies.subject: BCS601
case_studies.scenario: Compiler Lexical Analyzer for C-Subset Programming Language
entities: Source Code Characters: int main() { float x = 3.14; return 0; }
Tokens: <KEYWORD, int>, <ID, main>, <LPAREN>, <RPAREN>, <LBRACE>, <KEYWORD, float>, <ID, x>, <ASSIGN>, <NUM, 3.14>, <SEMICOLON>
relationships: Regular expressions specify token patterns
DFA recognizes lexemes with longest-match (maximal munch) rule
Symbol table stores identifiers and attributes
case_studies.inputs: High-level source code buffer with whitespace and comments
case_studies.outputs: Clean token stream passed directly to LR parser syntax analyzer
case_studies.constraints: Disambiguate keywords from identifiers; track line and column numbers for error reporting
case_studies.source: Aho Sethi Ullman Compilers Chapter 3 / BCS601 Module 1

case_studies.subject: BCS602
case_studies.scenario: Network Intrusion Detection System Using Decision Tree Classifier
entities: Network Connection Features: duration, protocol_type, service, flag, src_bytes, dst_bytes, count, serror_rate
Class Labels: Normal vs Attack (DoS, Probe, R2L, U2R)
relationships: Information Gain / Gini Impurity determines best feature split at each tree node
Post-pruning minimizes decision tree overfitting on noisy network traffic
case_studies.inputs: NSL-KDD benchmark training dataset containing 125,973 labeled connection records
case_studies.outputs: Interpretable if-then rule set achieving 94.2% detection rate with <1.5% false positive rate
case_studies.constraints: Real-time packet inspection requirement (<5 microseconds classification latency per packet)
case_studies.source: Bishop Machine Learning / Mitchell ML Chapter 3 / BCS602 M2

case_studies.subject: BCS613A
case_studies.scenario: Merkle Tree State Verification and SPV in Bitcoin Ledger
entities: Transactions: Tx0 through Tx7 (8 transactions in block)
Cryptographic Hashes: H(Tx0) through H(Tx7) using SHA-256 double hash
Block Header: Version, PreviousBlockHash, MerkleRoot, Timestamp, Bits (Difficulty), Nonce
relationships: Binary Merkle tree pairs adjacent hashes up to single 32-byte Merkle Root
Simplified Payment Verification (SPV) client verifies transaction presence using O(log N) authentication path
case_studies.inputs: Proof request for transaction Tx3 with 2000 transactions in block
case_studies.outputs: Audit path of only 11 intermediate hashes (352 bytes) instead of downloading entire 1.5MB block
case_studies.constraints: Any single-bit mutation in Tx3 invalidates root hash with cryptographic certainty
case_studies.source: Arvind Narayanan Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies Chapter 1
